title: LinkedIn Cuts Daily Spark Shuffle Fetch Failures from 750 to 20 with Apache Celeborn
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>LinkedIn deployed Apache Celeborn as a shared remote shuffle platform across most Spark and Flink workloads, reducing daily shuffle fetch failures from approximately 750 to 20. The deployment also lowered compute costs by 10%, improved application runtimes by 14%, and reduced shuffle costs per task by nearly 90% through dedicated storage, replication, and data-plane optimizations.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-privatelink-tunnel-endpoints/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794476042263.jpg"/><p>AWS has detailed tunnel endpoints, a PrivateLink endpoint type that gives a consumer VPC access to an entire network segment in another account rather than one resource at a time, over an overlapping address space and with consumer-initiated connections only. The consumer must wrap traffic in GENEVE; only TCP and DNS pass, and access logs cannot attribute traffic to a workload behind the endpoint.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/kubernetes-cassandra-eks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794921404342.jpg"/><p>Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet from legacy self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by re-pointing existing EBS volumes at new pods, rather than streaming data between nodes.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Datadog Brings Production Experimentation to AI Agent Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/datadog-ai-agent-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794408423767.jpg"/><p>Datadog is extending its Agent Observability platform with Online Experiments, allowing engineering teams to compare AI agent versions against real production traffic rather than relying exclusively on predefined evaluation datasets.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Ten Years On, Google Updates the SRE Book for the AI Era
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-sre-book-ai-era/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794674690062.jpg"/><p>Google has announced a completely rewritten second edition of Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems, ten years after the original book was published by O'Reilly Media. The update reframes SRE around modern cloud architectures, platform engineering and AI workloads, while retaining the discipline's original emphasis on applying software engineering to operations.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes Put Each EKS Pod in its Own MicroVM with One RuntimeClass Field
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-nitro-sandboxes-eks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794301940782.jpg"/><p>AWS has launched Nitro Sandboxes, running each opted-in EKS pod, ECS task or EC2 workload in its own Firecracker microVM with a separate kernel, enabled by one runtimeClassName field at no extra charge. A confidential mode adds attestation-gated key release. The documentation lists the trade-offs: no GPU passthrough, at most five sandboxes per vCPU, and half the compute on SMT instances.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Alpine Linux Users Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/alpine-linux-openssh-sshhole/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794610199233.jpg"/><p>A recently disclosed vulnerability in OpenSSH lets an unauthenticated attacker log into accounts that should have no usable password. The issue, named *sshole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158, affects Linux systems running OpenSSH with the musl C library and which don't use PAM. Security researchers now report that attackers are exploiting it in the wild.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Cloudflare Introduces Private Origins for Application Services
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cloudflare-private-origins/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793395278236.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently made Application Services for Private Origins generally available, allowing public traffic to reach applications hosted on private networks without exposing their IP addresses or opening inbound firewall ports. Private-to-private connectivity is not yet supported.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Google Cloud Moves the Compute Engine API to Immutable Date-Based Versions
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/compute-engine-api-versioning/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794296072866.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has made date-based versioning of the Compute Engine API generally available, replacing the single mutable /v1 surface with immutable quarterly snapshots such as 2026-09-01, selected per request with a header or query parameter. New versions can change defaults, error formats, and IAM checks without touching /v1 callers, a model Azure Resource Manager and Stripe have used for years.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Netflix Turns Operational Data into a Knowledge Graph for AI-Driven Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/netflix-ai-driven-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793693699423.jpg"/><p>Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: The Influence Toolkit
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/bbc-software-architecture-influence/en/mediumimage/henry-wilson-medium-1792653480613.jpg"/><p>Henry Wilson shares actionable tools from the BBC Sounds re-architecture to help senior engineering leaders drive technical strategy. He discusses building buy-in, navigating active resistors, using RFCs and ADRs, and balancing tradeoffs - showing that effective software architecture is fundamentally about communication, relationship-building, and organizational influence.</p> <i>By Henry Wilson</i>

title: Azure Logic Apps Standard Gets a Local CLI in Preview
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/logic-apps-local-cli/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793791837422.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released a public preview of the logicapp extension for the Azure CLI, adding local project creation, workflow authoring, a runtime lifecycle, connector management, run inspection, and test scaffolding for Logic Apps Standard, work that previously required the VS Code extension. The product team pitches the terminal surface as determinism for AI-assisted development.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: LinkedIn Replaces Argo CD with a Custom GitOps Engine for Kubernetes Deployments
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/kubernetes-argocd-linkedin/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794414453878.jpg"/><p>In a recent post, LinkedIn revealed it has replaced Argo CD with its own GitOps engine. This new system deploys applications across over 250 Kubernetes clusters. It supports more than 4,000 services and manages over 100,000 deployments each week.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows Generally Available with Isolation and Budget Controls
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-agentic-workflows-ga/en/headerimage/header-1793990975266.jpeg"/><p>GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available, running coding agents in GitHub Actions with read-only defaults and separately scoped write jobs. Those protections do not cover direct write permissions or custom jobs, so they depend on how each workflow is configured.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Presentation: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/opentelemetry-queue-observability/en/mediumimage/julian-oli-medium-1792652839179.jpg"/><p>Oli Lane and Julian Wreford share how Gearset replaced guesswork in distributed asynchronous queues with OpenTelemetry tracing. They explain why traditional metrics fall short, how to implement user-centric SLOs based on latency distributions, and share practical debugging tips to help senior developers, software architects, and engineering leaders improve system reliability and team culture.</p> <i>By Julian Wreford, Oli Lane</i>
